body:
### The problem

The parameters of an arrow function are counted only when it is assigned to a
name with parentheses, `const f = (a, b) => ...`. In every other form the
parameter count is 0:

```ts
const total = list.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.price, 0);
const names = list.map(item => item.name);
const pick = flag ? (a, b) => a : null;
const sizes = list.map((x: Item, i: number): number => x.size * i);
```

```
$ lizard a.ts          # master, 01afe9c
       1      1      8      0       1 (anonymous)@1-1@a.ts
       1      1      4      0       1 (anonymous)@2-2@a.ts
       1      1      4      0       1 (anonymous)@3-3@a.ts
       1      1      6      0       1 (anonymous)@4-4@a.ts
```

The parentheses are read before `=>` tells that they hold parameters, and the
reader of a binding pattern that reads them kept the defaults but not the
names; a single parameter without parentheses was never read as a parameter;
and a return type dropped what the parentheses held before `=>`.

### What changes

`lizard_languages/javascript_bindings.py` and
`lizard_languages/typescript_states.py`. The binding reader now keeps the
first name of each element, skipping a type after `:`, and an arrow function
takes them as its parameters. A name right before `=>` is the parameter of
`x => x`. The return type of an arrow function keeps the parentheses before
it, and the parentheses in the branch of a ternary are read as the other
parentheses are. With the fix:

```
       1      1      8      2       1 (anonymous)@1-1@a.ts
       1      1      4      1       1 (anonymous)@2-2@a.ts
       1      1      4      2       1 (anonymous)@3-3@a.ts
       1      1      6      2       1 (anonymous)@4-4@a.ts
```

### How it is tested

`Test_ES6_arrow_function_parameters` in `test/test_languages/testES6.py`:
3 tests, all failing on `master` without the change. The full suite passes on
the branch: `python -m pytest test` gives 1668 passed, 7 skipped. pycodestyle
reports no new warnings in the changed files.

### What does not change

The defaults of the parameters and the conditions in them, which the binding
reader already counted, and the arrow functions assigned to a name with
parentheses.

Thanks for maintaining lizard and for taking the time to look at this.
title: Count the parameters of JavaScript/TypeScript arrow functions
